 Print The upcoming Naruto live-action movie may be taking fans back to the moment that truly tested Naruto Uzumaki as a young ninja. New details about the film’s reported storyline suggest that its first major adventure will draw from the early days of the beloved manga and anime. The project has already sparked debate over its casting choices and the ages of its central characters. Now, its reported plot offers a stronger clue about which part of Naruto’s journey could reach the big screen. Naruto live-action movie plot points to the first ninja mission 
 According to a report from Knight Edge Media, the film will follow Naruto as he takes on his first mission with Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno. The reported synopsis describes a routine assignment that quickly turns into a dangerous encounter, forcing the young ninja to face a power he does not fully understand. The synopsis reads: "The Naruto story unfolds in a breathtaking alternate universe, where every child dreams of becoming a ninja. We follow Naruto Uzumaki, an exceptionally gifted but challenging new recruit, as he’s assigned to his first mission alongside reluctant teammates Sasuke and Sakura. The mission turns into something far more dangerous and sinister than anticipated, and Naruto is forced to confront his inner demons – including the literal demon that’s revealed to be the root of his own power. " The description does not name the enemy or explain where the mission takes place. Still, it brings one of the franchise’s most memorable early storylines into focus. In the original manga and anime, Naruto’s first major assignment outside the village leads into the Land of Waves arc. The story introduces the dangerous rogue ninja Zabuza Momochi and his young companion, Haku. It also gives Naruto, Sasuke and Sakura their first serious test as a team. That storyline could offer the filmmakers a natural starting point. It has emotional stakes, intense fights and room to establish the bonds between the three young ninjas. However, the studio has not confirmed that Zabuza and Haku will appear in the movie. Naruto casting raises questions about character ages
 The film’s casting process has also left fans guessing about the adaptation’s timeline. In July, Lionsgate reportedly sought Asian actors aged 18 and older to portray Naruto, Sasuke and Sakura as 16-year-old characters. That initially suggested the movie might move the characters forward from their original ages of around 12. But a second casting call, reportedly issued two weeks ago, sought actors aged 13 to 15 for Naruto and Sakura. The change has created uncertainty about how old the characters will be in the finished film. No official explanation has clarified the different age requirements. Production is expected to begin in the United Kingdom early next year. Until Lionsgate shares more details, the first-mission storyline remains the clearest indication of the direction the live-action Naruto movie could take.
